title: Conversational protocol capture
why: Users can describe protocol intent naturally, but safe medical-adjacent changes require an explicit review and confirmation boundary.
demoStory: A user describes one supported change, reviews the exact proposal, confirms once, and sees the persisted protocol update.
outcome: A user can describe a protocol change naturally, review a safe proposal, and confirm it without silent writes.

gates.title: Capture intent
gates.startState: The assistant input is open and no draft mutation exists.
gates.happyPath: The user speaks or types one natural-language protocol request and sees the interpreted intent.
gates.observableResult: A reviewable interpretation appears without modifying the protocol.
gates.proof: The visible interpretation matches the transcript and contains no committed mutation.
edgeCases: Ambiguous compound or dose asks for clarification.
Unsupported intent preserves the user's original text.

gates.title: Review proposal
gates.startState: A supported intent has been interpreted.
gates.happyPath: The user sees the exact proposed changes, warnings, and unchanged fields before confirmation.
gates.observableResult: The proposal makes every pending mutation and safety warning legible.
gates.proof: Proposal UI and API payload agree field for field.
edgeCases: Unsafe values are blocked with an actionable explanation.

gates.title: Confirm mutation
gates.startState: A valid proposal is visible and unconfirmed.
gates.happyPath: The user confirms once and the approved change is persisted exactly once.
gates.observableResult: The proposal closes with a durable success receipt.
gates.proof: One confirmation produces one durable write and a success receipt.
edgeCases: Retry after a timeout remains idempotent.

gates.title: See updated protocol
gates.startState: The confirmed mutation has a success receipt.
gates.happyPath: The refreshed protocol reflects the confirmed change across the intended surfaces.
gates.observableResult: The updated value survives reload and appears on the agreed surfaces.
gates.proof: Persisted state and rendered state agree after reload.
edgeCases: A failed refresh retains the success receipt and offers retry.

guardrails: No protocol mutation occurs before explicit confirmation.
The first slice supports one bounded intent family and does not become a general chat agent.
Web/mobile parity is decided explicitly before the final gate closes.
nonGoals: More than one intent family in the first slice
decisions: Explicit confirmation remains the only mutation boundary.
deferredEdgeCases: Multi-intent utterances are deferred until single-intent accuracy is proven.
references: Current API and persistence contract trace

review.question: Is every gate user-observable and independently passable?
Can mocks, stubs, display-only controls, or missing persistence fake the demo?
Which omitted edge case would most likely break the story?
Do the guardrails fit the stated timebox?
Is an irreversible or high-risk product decision unresolved?
